items.title: UK banks are Europe’s biggest coal financiers, report finds
items.summary_raw:
Study says UK-based banks provided $8.3bn in coal financing in four years, with Barclays and HSBC leading rise

UK banks are Europe’s biggest financial backers of the global coal industry, providing billions of pounds in funding for the climate-wrecking fossil fuel in the past four years, according to a report.

The study found UK-based banks had provided $8.3bn (£6.2bn) in coal financing since Cop26 in Glasgow in 2021, when global leaders pledged to “phase down” coal use. This compared with $4.9bn from German banks and $3.4bn from French banks over the same period.

items.title: Rubio says Iran would 'blackmail the world' if it had a nuclear weapon
items.summary_raw:
Rubio says Iran would 'blackmail the world' if it had a nuclear weapon

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that if Iran had a nuclear weapon, it would use it to "blackmail the world and to kill people".

"It would control the straits, charge a toll, and decide who got energy and who did not," Rubio said during an interview with Fox News, and added that this could present an "unacceptable risk".

He also accused Tehran of using money received through sanctions relief or economic selling to build weapons and "export the revolution" rather than to "improve the lives of the Iranian people".

"They use the money to fund Hezbollah, they use the money to fund Hamas, they use the money to fund Shia militias in Iraq… they use the money to sponsor terrorism and assassination plots," Rubio said. <

items.summary_raw:

items.title: The Cyprus Issue at the Center of the Cyprus Federation Dinner
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK. Efforts to restart talks on the Cyprus issue, as well as the longstanding role of the Greek-American community in promoting Cyprus’ positions in Washington, were at the center of the annual dinner hosted by the Federation of Cypriot American Organizations on Friday evening, September 25, at Terrace on the Park. The event, held, as every year, in the presence of the government delegation of the Republic of Cyprus attending the U.N. General Assembly and headed by President Nikos Christodoulides, honored three members of the Cypriot-American community for their contributions. The Lifetime Achievement Award was presented to John Josephakis, NVIDIA’s Global Vice President of Sales and Business Development for High Performance Computing and Supercomputing. The Community Service Award was presented to Stavros Kamilaris, president of the Lampousa Cypriot American Association, and Despina Axiotakis, former executive director of the Cyprus-U.S. Chamber of Commerce, for her many years of service to the community.

items.title: Ex-Haniyeh Bodyguard Held in London
items.summary_raw:
A former bodyguard to Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh was granted asylum in Britain, later received permanent residency and became a British citizen, The Sunday Times reports.

Years later, he was arrested in London over a Hamas linked plot to attack Jewish and Israeli targets across Europe.

German prosecutors say he helped move weapons and recorded a masked claim of responsibility video.

He now remains in UK custody.

Saudi Arabia warned UN members Saturday that attempts to block Middle East waterways are a threat to global energy security and demanded the international community do more to defend freedom of navigation.

Since the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran in late February, Tehran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while its Houthi allies in Yemen have subsequently done the same in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Both waterways are vital routes for oil and gas exports.

items.summary_raw:
Israeli forces kill Palestinian in Gaza, arrest four farmers in West Bank

Israeli forces shot and killed a Palestinian man in the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, Wafa news agency reported, citing sources at Gaza City’s al-Shifa Hospital.

Wafa also reported that several Palestinians, including a child, were wounded in an Israeli drone attack on the outskirts of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, while eastern parts of the city came under Israeli artillery fire.

Israeli forces arrested four Palestinian farmers while they were harvesting olives on their land east of Tulkarem in the occupied West Bank, according to Wafa.

The farmers were working near the Israeli settlement of Einav when they were detained.

Wafa said more than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza by Israeli forces

The post came after The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had rejected Iran’s proposal, citing unnamed US officials.

The report said Trump was sceptical that Tehran would meet his demands and believed a renewed US bombing campaign was likely.

items.title: Greek Social Enterprise Enaleia Makes New York Debut at Climate Week 2026
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK – Greek social enterprise Enaleia, which works to reduce marine plastic pollution and promote sustainable fishing practices, made its New York debut this month at Climate Week NYC. Held September 21-28, Climate Week NYC brings together business leaders, policymakers, environmental organizations, and others for hundreds of events across New York focused on climate action and solutions. Representing Enaleia was Partnerships and Impact Coordinator Fani Sakellariou, who was also visiting New York for the first time. Speaking with The National Herald, Sakellariou reflected on the experience of representing the organization internationally and the opportunities her work has given her to see environmental initiatives and policymaking firsthand. “I’m extremely grateful to the whole team for sending me, and I’ve been very fortunate to have traveled a lot this year for work,” Sakellariou told TNH.

The post Greek Social Enterprise Enaleia Makes New York Debut at Climate Week 2026 appeared first on The National

items.title: Iran proposes plan to reopen Hormuz within seven days
items.summary_raw:
Iran proposes plan to reopen Hormuz within seven days

Araghchi met for talks on Tuesday with US President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff, and previously set out conditions for ending the war and reopening the vital energy shipping channel. 

"Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days," Araghchi said at the UN Friday.

"The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats, or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure.

"I can tell you if there is seriousness in the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared."

items.title: The Words of Climate, the Climate of Words: How We Talk about a Changing World
items.summary_raw:
Climate change is not purely an environmental or scientific issue. It is also a social, political and — less obviously — linguistic one. Science explains what is happening through indicators and figures and produces ominous of the Earth’s future. Yet society, politics and language largely determine how we perceive reality and, ultimately, how we choose to respond to it. And this may be one of the most critical challenges of our time. Language does not simply describe reality; it also shapes it. The shift from “climate change” to “climate crisis” or “climate collapse” is not merely a matter of vocabulary. Such choices appeal to the emotions of readers and listeners, foster fear, create a sense of urgency and make the need for action more pressing. Language thus becomes a lens through which reality is interpreted, influencing the way we understand the problem. This is why Linguistics[1] examines how the media and social networks talk about climate change through particular linguistic choices.

items.title: METLEN and Dolomiti Energia Inaugurate the Erchie BESS in Apulia
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - METLEN and Dolomiti Energia have inaugurated the new 25 MW/75 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Erchie, Apulia. Its commissioning marks the next milestone for a project first presented earlier this year, when the two companies signed a seven-year physical tolling agreement. Among the first arrangements of its kind in the Italian storage market, the agreement introduces an advanced commercial model that combines the long-term use of the infrastructure with the provision of critical flexibility to the electricity grid. Developed and delivered entirely by METLEN, the project supports the further integration of renewable energy sources and contributes to strengthening the stability of Italy’s electricity system.

The post METLEN and Dolomiti Energia Inaugurate the Erchie BESS in Apulia appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: ‘We don’t have time for more promises’: the Croatian town that took on an illegal waste dump
items.summary_raw:
After years of illegal mass flytipping in Gospić, fed-up residents decided to take matters into their own hands

“Gospić is our home,” Željka Šikić shouted to a crowd of 40,000 people outside the Croatian parliament earlier this month. The slogan is the name of a campaign she helped to set up to protest against the illegal dumping of waste in Gospić, a town in the mountainous Lika region of central Croatia.

Between 2022 and 2024, waste was illegally abandoned at several sites in the town. At one of the biggest, just 50 metres from Šikić’s home, an estimated 35,000 tonnes of waste, some of it hazardous, was dumped and buried.

items.title: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan defended the Mecca Alliance against criticism that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were its “first test.”  Fidan compared it to NATO, asking for…
items.summary_raw: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan defended the Mecca Alliance against criticism that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were its “first test.”  Fidan compared it to NATO, asking former U.S. Ambassador to Türkiye James Jeffrey how many times NATO’s Article 5 had been invoked. After Jeffrey answered “only once,” Fidan said it was unfair to judge a new defense alliance using a 10-year conflict as evidence that it does not work.  “Nobody criticizes NATO as a paper tiger. But when it comes to a newborn defense alliance, they point to a 10-year crisis in Yemen and say, ‘Look, this is not working.’ We have only just started.”

items.title: Trump Administration Asks the Supreme Court to Allow Quick Third-Country Deportations to Continue
items.summary_raw:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump's administration asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to again clear the way for continued quick deportations of immigrants to third countries where they have no ties. The government asked for an immediate halt to lower court orders finding that people must have the chance to object before the U.S. government deports them to countries other than their homelands. The justices allowed the deportation flights to continue when the case came before them last year. Since then, an appeals court has upheld a Boston-based judge’s final ruling that migrants must have a meaningful chance to argue a third-country deportation would put them in danger of persecution or torture. The order doesn't completely prohibit deportations to third countries, but it adds new requirements. The Trump administration says that creates unworkable delays and has already led to the cancellation of a flight carrying 70 people with criminal convictions to three different countries.

Hundreds of thousands are expected to die, millions to go hungry. This is not just about weather patterns, but about injustice

Some warnings are so grave that it is almost impossible to fully comprehend them. The descriptions of a super-sized, “Godzilla-level” El Niño already heating our planet would sound hyperbolic were they not issuing from eminent scientists. They say that the weather pattern, which occurs roughly every two to seven years, may be the strongest in at least a millennium. With its peak yet to come, the temperature rise in the Pacific Ocean has already surpassed the previous high.

The consequence will be huge amounts of heat in an atmosphere already experiencing frighteningly higher temperatures due to the human-caused climate crisis. Next year is almost certain to be the hottest on record globally, breaking this year’s record. The World Food Programme has warned that 50 million people are likely to be pushed into acute hunger. items.title: Gavin Newsom condemns Democrats’ ‘climate hushing’, predicts Trump’s downfall and expects AOC to run in 2028
items.summary_raw:
Democrats must show links of climate shocks to ‘kitchen table’ issues, California governor says

It’s a mistake for Democratic politicians not to talk about climate change, and the reason they don’t is “because they don’t know how to talk about it”, the California governor, Gavin Newsom, said on Wednesday in an interview with the Guardian and the global journalism collaboration Covering Climate Now.

Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meeting and New York Climate Week, Newsom also predicted that the midterm elections in November would bring “the end of Donald Trump’s presidency as we know it”. To prevent Trump from stealing those elections, voters must turn out in such overwhelming numbers that he “couldn’t possibly contest” the outcome. If the US president nevertheless declares a national emergency or otherwise attempts to invalidate the results, Newsom said, then “we the people have to step up. The courts have to intervene. Congress has to do its job and stand up for the rule of law.”
